Five animated films have each won two Oscars. They are The Incredibles (2004), Up (2009), Toy Story 3 (2010), Frozen (2013), and Coco (2017). All five won the Academy Award for best animated feature. The Incredibles also won for best sound editing, Up won for best original score, and the rest won for best original song. results.title: Will Wildwood join these historic stop-motion films in Oscar history?
results.content: The end of the 1980s was marked by two exceptional claymation shorts, both from Nick Park and Aardman Animations. Park’s "Creature Comforts" (1989) and the Wallace & Gromit-introducing "A Grand Day Out" (1989) were both nominated for Best Animated Short Film at the 1990 Academy Awards, with "Creature Comforts" winning. Subsequent Wallace & Gromit shorts "The Wrong Trousers" (1993) and "A Close Shave" (1995) went on to win the prize for their respective years. Aardman’s short "Wat’s Pig" was [...] Two other world-class live-action directors have joined the stop-motion train, advancing the art form. Wes Anderson’s Fantastic Mr. Fox (2009) gained numerous fans for its charm, unique look, and stellar vocal performances, competing for Best Animated Feature and Best Original Score. Anderson returned to the medium for 2018’s Isle of Dogs, which received the same pair of nominations at the 91st Academy Awards in 2019. Guillermo del Toro took to the medium in 2022 for Pinocchio, a stellar [...] The 1970s marked a high-profile chapter for claymation, with California Raisins creator Will Vinton’s short "Closed Mondays" (co-directed with Bob Gardiner) winning the Academy Award for Best Animated Short Film in 1975. The use of stop-motion as a special effect hit new heights with George Lucas’ original Star Wars trilogy.
